stem:
The diagram shows line AB, point P not on AB, and three trial lines through P labelled m, n, and k.

Which claim correctly identifies a line through P parallel to AB?

options.text: Line m, because it keeps the same direction as AB and does not meet AB.
Any line through the given point P is already parallel to AB.
Point P is what produces line AB, so drawing line k through P creates AB first.
Line n, because it meets AB at right angles and perpendicular marks settle parallelism.

teacher.key_rationale: A line through P parallel to AB keeps AB's direction and never meets AB. Point P alone does not make every line parallel, P does not produce AB, and a perpendicular through P is not parallel.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle figure as line AB, external point P, and trial lines m (parallel), n (perpendicular), and k (secant).
